methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.

scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.

actual_scope: For each of all 112 fixed T740 port recipes at owner replica zero, test every per-axis support assignment over its 20 residual-child slots that conserves the number of copies of that axis, obeys child orthogonality and the rank-51 cap, and leaves translations, hosts, chronology, bridges and native events fixed. There are 72 distinct residual axes per port. Exact eight-stream operator equality is checked at each axis character, which isolates that vector from every other distinct axis.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a quantified interface implication; this refines it to the unresolved repeated-copy case left by PR3190-distinct-axis-basis-isolation. Its orthogonal-character argument handles distinct moved axes but does not separate multiple transfers of the same axis. Instead of adding more singleton checks, this work exhausts every balanced occupancy pattern for each axis using an exact meet-in-the-middle matrix equality test. It is a finite fixed-source obstruction, not an all-size claim.
bottleneck_link: A rank redistribution can improve the recursive moment only if it preserves the exact physical operator. This closes all same-dictionary, per-axis copy redistributions for the fixed owner-zero T740 schedule; reaching a larger kappa therefore requires changing the axis dictionary, an intervening interaction, or another priced part of the mechanism.
stop_rule: Authenticate the exact 112-port T740 inputs; verify all 20 hosted/residual frames and the 72-axis orthogonality/isolation conditions per port; exhaust all balanced occupancy patterns for each axis with exact Gaussian-integer meet-in-the-middle equality; direct-replay the positive mask controls; stop if every nonempty balanced pattern changes the operator. Do not expand to changed axes, translations, bridges, replicas, or a supplier/kappa claim.
evidence: The two registered receipts cover all 112 owner-zero port recipes and 8,064 isolated port-axis pairs. They count 14,089,152 copy-balanced occupancy patterns (including each empty baseline), 5,730,304 exact meet states and 26,880 patterns surviving the six-column signature for direct full-matrix replay; every replay differs from baseline and the full exact-equality count is zero. All distinct residual vectors are pairwise orthogonal and self-odd in every port. The port-zero 16-mask control, exact event/segment factorization checks, source pins and journal-preimage mutation rejection pass. No kappa or selected-frontier improvement is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can changing the residual axis vectors themselves, together with one actual bridge interaction, create an exactly cancelling rank transfer at a lower complete cost?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This search keeps the 72-vector orthogonal dictionary fixed. A support reassignment cannot help; a structural kappa gain would need a new phase dictionary or an altered interleaving whose bridge conjugation couples those phases.
open_questions.first_step: Start with one four-axis orthogonal-frame move on a two-dimensional or four-dimensional subspace adjacent to a single bridge: derive the resulting Z/4 phase-polynomial difference, solve the exact 8-by-8 Gaussian-integer intertwining equation for the changed bridge, and price the changed ranks, bridge/frame work and restoration before widening the search.
open_questions.blocked_by: No source-supported cheap bridge rewrite or full changed-event invoice is known. The existing one-site chart and fixed-interaction obstructions do not certify this changed-interaction model.

open_questions.why_it_matters: The receipt freezes translations and hosting; either can alter the phase at the isolating character or the legal destination set.
